# use-kimi-on-cursor

> Open-source Windows desktop app that lets you use Moonshot Kimi K2.6 inside Cursor IDE.

## What it is

Kimi Cursor Gateway bridges Cursor (which expects OpenAI-compatible APIs) to Moonshot's Kimi K2.6 API. It runs a local Rust/Axum gateway, exposes it via Cloudflare Quick Tunnel (public HTTPS), and provides a Tauri desktop UI for setup and monitoring.

Repository: https://github.com/Lolner95/use-kimi-on-cursor

## Primary use case

Developers who want to use Kimi (Moonshot AI) as the model behind Cursor for code generation, refactoring, debugging, and Agent mode with MCP tools.

## Quick setup

1. Get API key from https://platform.moonshot.ai
2. Install Kimi Cursor Gateway from GitHub Releases
3. Paste Moonshot key in app wizard, start gateway
4. In Cursor Settings → Models:
   - OpenAI API Key: gateway key from app (NOT Moonshot key)
   - Override OpenAI Base URL: ON
   - Base URL: https URL from app ending in /v1
   - Model: gpt-5-high-max (maps to kimi-k2.6)

## Why a tunnel is required

Cursor blocks requests to private/local URLs (127.0.0.1). The app uses Cloudflare Quick Tunnel to provide a public HTTPS endpoint.

## Key technical details

- Platform: Windows 10/11
- Stack: Tauri 2, Rust, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
- Local gateway: 127.0.0.1:4001
- Upstream: api.moonshot.ai
- Model: kimi-k2.6 (256K context)
- Moonshot API key encrypted with Windows DPAPI
- Gateway sanitizes Cursor payloads: tool names, roles, streaming, thinking mode

```

```
